title: DCT2000: Allow any PDU to be dissected if it lacks lower layers.
description:
There are traffic dumps that only include the PDU payload
without lower layer information.  This commit allows any
dissector to be embedded in the DCT2000 as a protocol name.
tshark/wireshark will decode it despite having no lower
layer information.

The change allows a DCT2000 protocol field to look for a
dissector.

Example:

```
Session Transcript (format 3.1)
December 6, 2020     16:45:20.5185
LTE-RRC.1/lte_rrc.dl_dcch/1/// r tm 22.5695 l $2c02
S1AP.1/s1ap/1/// s tm 23.3926 l
$001700130000020063000608023d7c00830002400202a0
```

How are you creating these messages?  Are you just using the DCT2000 file format out of convenience?

Almost every eNodeB, gNb, RNC... dumps PDUs in hex format without lower layer protocols. the hex dumps lacks RLC, MAC, IP, SCTP.... they only dump the hex value of the PDU. Converting the hex dumps to dct2000 is fairly trivial (even an awk script can do it). 

~~PCAP or PCAPNG formats are not suitable per se, the list of allowed encapsulation types use the full stack. There is the DLT trick to allow encapsulating PDUs in pcap, but it's limited to 16 protocols.~~ Edit after this thread feedback. PCAP can be used for the same purposes using DLT_WIRESHARK_UPPER_PDU. 

on the other hand, DCT2000 format allows to define the protocol / dissector quite easily in the second field. This change looks for a dissector with the same name as the protocol in the second field.

The change do not impact the file format, and previous dct2000 files will continue to work. The change allows more protocols to be decoded.

> Almost every eNodeB, gNb, RNC... dumps PDUs in hex format without lower layer protocols. the hex dumps lacks RLC, MAC, IP, SCTP.... they only dump the hex value of the PDU. Converting the hex dumps to dct2000 is fairly trivial (even an awk script can do it).

I.e., you're just using the DCT2000 file format out of convenience.

> PCAP or PCAPNG formats are not suitable per se, the list of allowed encapsulation types use the full stack.

To what "list of allowed encapsulation types" are you referring?  [The current list of encapsulation types for pcap and pcapng](https://www.tcpdump.org/linktypes.html)?

Edit after this thread feedback. ~~Right, I'm referring to the encapsulation types for pcap and pcapng at the tcpdump [linktypes](https://www.tcpdump.org/linktypes.html). As far as I know the only way in pcapng to add PDUs without lower layers is using the DLT_USER0-DLT_USER15. Unfortunately, the DLT_USER is limited to 16 protocols.~~

This comment has been strikedout. PCAP can read PDUs without lower layers when the DLT is DLT_WIRESHARK_UPPER_PDU and setting the EXP_PDU_TAG_PROTO_NAME to the dissector name.

> As far as I know the only way in pcapng to add PDUs without lower layers

What lower layers?  If you mean "link layers", there's LINKTYPE_RAW for packets where the lowest layer is IP (v4 or v6), there's LINKTYPE_MTP2_WITH_PHDR and LINKTYPE_MTP2 for packets where the lowest layer is MTP2, there's LINKTYPE_MTP3 for packets where the lowest layer is MTP3, there's LINKTYPE_SCCP for packets where the lowest layer is SCCP. and there's LINKTYPE_SCTP for packets where the lowest layer is SCTP.

Those work with both pcap and pcapng.

None of those linktypes (LINKTYPE_RAW, LINKTYPE_MTP2_WITH_PHDR, LINKTYPE_MTP2, LINKTYPE_MTP3, LINKTYPE_SCTP) are suitable. Because the PDU has no IP, TCP, UDP, SCTP, MTP2 or MTP3.  

Example of the PDUs: 
   * S1AP is dumped without without SCTP, IP, eth
   * X2 is dumped without without SCTP, IP, eth
   * RRC UL-DCCH is dumped without  PDPC, RLC, MAC
DLT_WIRESHARK_UPPER_PDU seems suitable for your needs: I use it for the exact same kind of use case as yours.

Thanks for the suggestion Pascal. 

Your suggestion works. I will edit my comments about PCAP, because they are not true. 

On the other hand, there are some equipment around that creates text dumps in dct2000 (text format). 
This commit enables wireshark to read those text files if they use the dissector name in the text protocol field.

You already have the exported PDU format specified [here](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/epan/exported_pdu.h) and that has its own DLT value allowing to specify a dissector on a per packet basis.

Thanks for the suggestion Pascal. 

The exported PDU format works, i have tested it a few minutes ago. But I have a doubt regarding the linktype it uses. From (pcap-common.c)[https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/wiretap/pcap-common.c]

`        { 252,          WTAP_ENCAP_WIRESHARK_UPPER_PDU},`

It uses the linktype=252 and encap_value of 155. 
The linktype=252 is not registered in the [linktypes](https://www.tcpdump.org/linktypes.html). Maybe there is a risk of being reused in the future. 

Going back to the DCT2000 text format. 

Nevertheless, with the mention of pcap I have deviated the conversation from the purpose of the commit. 
The commit does for DCT2000 the same as exported-pdu with EXP_PDU_TAG_PROTO_NAME. It looks for a dissector name defined per packet.

THe numbers we use were officially allocated by the tcpdump project. I do not know why it does not appear in the page you link, but it will not be reused.

I'm not sure hacking the DCT2000 protocol format your your specific need is something wanted in the first place, thus my known to work suggestion.

I have edited all my comments, so if somebody reads this thread, he knows how to proceed. 

I'm sure that for future projects that I have 100% control I will use the PCAP format with DLT_WIRESHARK_UPPER_PDU as you have suggested. Really useful comment. 

But there are some files out there, generated by other equipment, that are in text format that can be trivially transformed to DCT2000 file format. This change allows to read them and will not impact existing DCT2000 files. 

Is there any chance of having this merge request approved?

Hijacking the dissector of another product and modifying its behavior for your convenience does not sound like a good idea IMHO. But on the other hand the change is rather minimal.

I do not work for Ixia / Keysight so I will not take the final decision. @martin.r.mathieson, as the original dissector author, are you ok with the proposal?

> None of those linktypes (LINKTYPE_RAW, LINKTYPE_MTP2_WITH_PHDR, LINKTYPE_MTP2, LINKTYPE_MTP3, LINKTYPE_SCTP) are are suitable.

Nobody said they were.

They *are*, however, counterexamples to assertions that "the only way in pcapng to add PDUs without lower layers is using the DLT_USER0-DLT_USER15", because they're LINKTYPE_ values without a link layer and, in many cases, without, for example, a network layer.

> S1AP is dumped without without SCTP, IP, eth

So propose LINKTYPE_S1AP to tcpdump-workers@lists.tcpdump.org.

> X2 is dumped without without SCTP, IP, eth

So propose LINKTYPE_X1 to tcpdump-workers@lists.tcpdump.org.

> RRC UL-DCCH is dumped without PDPC, RLC, MAC

Lather, rinse, repeat.

Or perhaps [GSMTAP](http://cgit.osmocom.org/libosmocore/tree/include/osmocom/core/gsmtap.h) could be use for, at least, RRC UL-DCCH.

thanks for the comments. 

The suggestion from  Pascal Quantin is the way to go if using pcap. 
I write here for reference if somebody needs it in the future. 

- encapsulation mode WTAP_ENCAP_WIRESHARK_UPPER_PDU
- link-layer 252 
- Tag EXP_PDU_TAG_PROTO_NAME (12) with value equals to the PDU dissector.  

But there are equipment that generates dct2000 hex dumps in text format. 
This commit enables a way to read those dumps.

I think Pascals suggestion is the way to go, by using exported PDU when tranforming logs to a file
readable by wireshark meta information in the form of tags or comments can be added too.
Even better if the node itself could write signaling data in pcapng format :-)
My 2 cents
Anders

You are right, Pascal's comments are the way to go. I have strikedout my comments about PCAP. 

As you point out, it's better if the node could  write signaling data in pcap format. But there are equipment that create text files. This commit allows to read those files (with a trivial transformation before).

The dct2000 format, being text, is convenient.  I sometimes write scripts to scour product logs for packets and write them to a dct2000 log, then you can edit the payloads and immediately reload in Wireshark, etc.

There is also the 'log3gpp' wiretap module and dissector which seems to have a similar goal.  I have never used it, but it looks as though it could be extended to support some of the more recent protocols you mentioned as examples.

The dct2000 format is still in use, and people often load fairly large logs, so I would be reluctant to slow this down by doing lots of doomed protocol name lookups.  I wouldn't object though if you added a preference that defaulted to off to avoid this lookup for us.

thank you for the feedback. 

I have added a preference to check if the dissector lookup shall be done. The preference is false by default.  

tshark shows now this text when invoked as `tshark -G defaultprefs`
```
# When set, it uses the protocol name to find a dissector with the same name. The DCT2000 protocol name and the dissector name shall match.
# TRUE or FALSE (case-insensitive)
#dct2000.use_protocol_name_as_dissector_name: FALSE
```

And wireshark display the attached image.![wireshark-preference](/uploads/89f688e915a184707ebdcc8a8468602e/wireshark-preference.png)

DCT2000: Allow any PDU to be dissected.

There are traffic dumps that only include the PDU payload
without lower layer information.  This commit allows any
dissector to be embedded in the DCT2000 as a protocol name.
tshark/wireshark will decode it despite having no lower
layer information.

The change allows a DCT2000 protocol field to look for a
dissector.

The change can be enabled or disabled with the preference
dct2000.use_protocol_name_as_dissector_name and it defaults
to FALSE.

Example:

LTE-RRC.1/lte_rrc.dl_dcch/1/// r tm 22.5695 l $2c02
S1AP.1/s1ap/1/// s tm 23.3926 l
